title: Intersection of Three Sorted Arrays
statement: You are given three integer arrays `arr1`, `arr2` and `arr3`, each sorted in strictly increasing order (so no array repeats a value). Return a list, in increasing order, of the integers that appear in all three arrays. When no integer is common to all three, return an empty list.
signature: List<Integer> arraysIntersection(int[] arr1, int[] arr2, int[] arr3)
notes:
## Intuition

Checking each value of `arr1` against the other two arrays works but scans them again and again, O(n²) overall. Because all three arrays are sorted, a single left-to-right sweep is enough: keep one pointer per array, and whenever the three current values differ, every value smaller than the largest of them cannot be shared, so its pointer can move on.

## Approach

1. Start `i`, `j` and `k` at the front of `arr1`, `arr2` and `arr3`.
2. While all three pointers are inside their arrays, compare the current values.
3. If they are all equal, add the value to `result` and advance all three pointers.
4. Otherwise find `largest` of the three, and advance every pointer whose value is below it; those values can never meet the largest one.
5. Once any array runs out, nothing else can be common, so return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr1 = [1,2,3,4,5]`, `arr2 = [1,2,5,7,9]`, `arr3 = [1,3,4,5,8]`. All start at `1`, so `1` is recorded. Next the values are `2, 2, 3`: `largest = 3`, so `i` and `j` move. Then `3, 5, 3`: `i` and `k` move. Then `4, 5, 4`: again `i` and `k` move. Now `5, 5, 5` match, so `5` is recorded and `i` leaves `arr1`. The result is `[1, 5]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n1 + n2 + n3): each step advances at least one pointer.
- Space: O(1) apart from the output.

## Pitfalls

- Advance only the pointers below the largest value; moving the pointer at the largest value can skip a match.
- Stop as soon as one array is exhausted; reading past its end compares against `undefined`.
- The arrays are strictly increasing, so no duplicates need to be filtered from the answer.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i`, `j`, `k` | current positions in `arr1`, `arr2`, `arr3` |
| `largest` | the biggest of the three current values |
| `result` | the shared values found so far, in order |
